entities.name: Rat periodontitis
observations: Repeated oral polybacterial infection or ligature-induced periodontitis in rats increases systemic or distant-organ oxidative-stress markers.
Evidence includes serum, liver, and kidney oxidative-stress measurements.

entities.name: Alendronate
observations: In a rat polybacterial periodontitis model, alendronate inhibited the infection-associated increase in serum oxidative stress.

entities.name: Bis-enoxacin
observations: In a rat polybacterial periodontitis model, bis-enoxacin inhibited serum oxidative-stress elevation and was more effective than alendronate.

entities.name: Serum oxidative stress
observations: Rat polybacterial periodontitis increased serum oxidative stress index approximately five-fold versus sham controls, with higher total oxidant status and lower total antioxidant status; P<0.001.
Alendronate and bis-enoxacin attenuated the periodontitis-associated serum oxidative-stress increase.

entities.name: Extraoral oxidative injury
observations: Ligature-induced rat periodontitis increased liver ROS and MDA and decreased liver SOD and GSH, with structural liver injury.
The same model class increased kidney ROS and MDA and decreased kidney GSH, SOD, mitochondrial membrane potential, Nrf2, and PGC-1α; no antiresorptive was tested.

entities.name: Antiresorptive evidence gap
observations: No retrieved rat-periodontitis study demonstrated systemic oxidative-stress reduction with zoledronic acid, pamidronate, or denosumab.
The direct evidence is limited to alendronate and bis-enoxacin in one polybacterial infection study.
